doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: War years and return to New York
title: 1939 Paris, the union dispute, and recording with Django
summary: Ellington played Paris rather than London because of the British and American union standoff; Dance met Django at a Rex Stewart session.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I could always read French you know, but I could never speak it well. But then I was going to come back to New York, but in 1939 I saw Ellington again. They didn’t play London. I think by that time there was the struggle between the two unions you know. The British union felt British bands should come here in reciprocation. The American union didn’t want them. But Duke played in Paris.
Let me ask you about that. Because I thought it was the other way around, that the British union didn’t want the American bands coming.

No. Well the American union was in a much stronger position. There were only — the only band with any international recognition in England was Jack Hylton’s. I don’t think any other really had much of a name before Word War II. I mean Ambrose had a good band but they hadn’t anybody that would be known in America. Whereas in England and Europe, they knew many of these American bands, and they’d been playing there. I mean I remember I also heard Hal Kemp’s band. I think Bunny Berigan was in that band and I never knew it. But no I think the call was not entirely justified, but was our loss. When

Duke played in Paris I remember going there. That was when I first met Django, when we had a record session under Rex Stewart’s name, which came out very well. But then there was six rather bleak years while the war lasted before I could come back. And my wife being an OSS and had gone to Africa and Italy and — my wife-to-be that is — I had to come back in 1946 to pursue my suit you see. But it was a rather confusing time because it changed so much.
